title: Thanking
subtitle: 감사
review: Written by Claude. The Korean and the romanization have not been checked by a Korean speaker. English support only: no Burmese lines were written. Check before recording audio.

categories.desc: Two polite standards and a friendlier form.
cards:
감사합니다.

The safe, polite thank you, for anyone.

고맙습니다.

Just as polite. A native Korean word, and a little warmer.

고마워요.

Polite but friendly. To close friends: Gomawo.

Oneul jeongmal gamsahaetseumnida.
오늘 정말 감사했습니다.
Thank you very much for today.

categories.desc: Korean answers to thanks are modest: mostly a way of saying no.
cards:
천만에요.

The textbook answer. Rare in daily speech, where people say Anieyo.

별말씀을요.

Polite and modest: 'what a thing to say'.

Jeongmal gamsahamnida. — Byeolmalsseumeullyo.
정말 감사합니다. — 별말씀을요.
Thank you very much. — Don't mention it.

Dowajwoseo gomawoyo. — Mwollyo.
도와줘서 고마워요. — 뭘요.
I'm the one who should thank you.

저야말로 감사합니다.

Jeoyamallo: 'I, rather than you'. It hands the thanks back.

Oneul gamsahaetseumnida. — Jeoyamallo gamsahamnida.
오늘 감사했습니다. — 저야말로 감사합니다.
Thank you for today. — Thank you.

categories.desc: Set phrases that carry thanks: for food, for work, for help.
cards:
잘 먹겠습니다.

'I will eat well.' Thanks to whoever cooked or is paying.

Masitgetda! Jal meokgetseumnida.
맛있겠다! 잘 먹겠습니다.
That looks delicious! Thank you for the meal.

잘 먹었습니다.

After eating: 'I ate well.'

Jal meogeotseumnida. Jeongmal masisseosseoyo.
잘 먹었습니다. 정말 맛있었어요.
Thank you for the meal. It was really delicious.

수고하세요.

Said as you leave a shop or a taxi: thanks to someone who is still working.
Thanks to you, it went well.

덕분에 잘 됐어요.

Deokbune: thanks to you.

Siheom eottaesseoyo? — Deokbune jal dwaesseoyo.
시험 어땠어요? — 덕분에 잘 됐어요.
How was the exam? — Thanks to you, it went well.
